# What this records

After merge commit `1205e347473461266055a1532eabbbca7c0b4b95`, a fresh VPS2 MCP process ran the
locked 50 query graph off versus one hop attribution benchmark on 2026-09-12. The query file
digest was `63d290a61189758a88b47bfed981ae1331d87fc004b752d632c1f5b58f5aa192`, with generation
`gen_6559b6dbacfc4bc2847b65005f1ba1d4`.

One hop server p95 was 1283.636 ms versus 598.949 ms for graph off, so the secondary availability
guard failed at 2.143 times baseline. Warm projection p95 was 0.019 ms and warm adjacency p95 was
0 ms. One hop query embedding p95 was 232.690 ms, with 3.02 times the graph off p95 database
transferred bytes. The likely highest ROI optimization is reusing the baseline query vector before
graph first expansion performs its own embedding.

The note above flags that `*_recall_desktop_pgdata` pairs survive their worktrees and that eight
belonged to checkouts that no longer existed. Doing that cleanup produced two false positives,

## The case for Redis that survives

# RE-call: pricing a store backend swap (Redis), 2026-08-04

**Question asked:** can RE-call's RAG be adapted to Redis, and would performance improve?
**Answer: possible, not a drop-in, and NOT justified by latency.** PR
[#189](https://github.com/GiulioDER/RE-call/pull/189) merged as `8147d96`.

## The number that decides it

20,050 chunks, bge-small, local reranker, 50 queries x 2 repeats, warm. Artifact:
`results/store_latency/chunks_20k/splits.json` (stamped with `stack` + `generated_at`).

| candidate_k | rerank | total | store | **store share** |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 20 | no | 37.1 ms | 16.6 | 44.7% |
| 20 | yes | 1,605 ms | 32.9 | 2.1% |
| 250 | no | 266.0 ms | 242.4 | 91.1% |
| **250** | **yes** | **18,205 ms** | 480.8 | **2.6%** |

🔑 **The cross-encoder is 17.7 s of an 18.2 s query in the SHIPPED best config.** A store that
cost zero would take 18.2 s to 17.7 s. The cheap levers are reranker cost and `candidate_k`, not
the engine.

🔑 **The 91.1% row prices a KNOB, not a backend.** At `candidate_k=250` the dense leg runs at
`hnsw.ef_search = min(k x multiplier, 1000)` against 80 at k=20, which is what takes it from
10.5 ms to 236.9 ms. Any ANN backend re-pays that walk rather than removing it. Tune ef_search
before considering a port.

🔑 **Shares are robust, absolute latency is not.** Two runs, same host, same seed: the reranked
TOTAL swung +21% (15,075 to 18,205 ms) while the shares moved at most 0.31 points. This is why
the artifact needed `stack` and `generated_at`, and why RESULTS.md warns its latency columns are
comparable only within one table.

Four rounds: 9 parallel auditors, a differential review, two architect gate rounds. Each round
found defects in the previous round's FIXES. Every defect biased the store share DOWNWARD, i.e.

## Meta-finding

**Isolation premium is conditional on signal-quality threshold.**

- **Above threshold (high-conviction signals): isolated > clustered.**
  Mechanism: the first big move after quiet captures maximum private information; subsequent moves leak / are partially priced.
- **Below threshold (low-conviction signals): clustered > isolated.**
  Mechanism: small/routine signals carry no info alone; they become informative only when many align (cluster = consensus). Classical Cohen-Malloy-Pomorski 2012.

- **Always `--pool-size 4`** for backfill and launch runs. Direct connection mode loses the local
  Postgres connection during sparse backfill, because cursor reads and sparse writes share one held
  connection.

  500K-document corpus needs a rented GPU and a backgrounded launch.
- **Indexing progress is invisible to SQL while the process runs.** External counts returned zero
  even as the log printed `index wrote ...`. Trust `tail -f` on the run log, not a `SELECT count(*)`.

## Reusable test template

For ANY new shadow candidate, run a 3-quadrant test:

```
                 isolated    clustered
high-conviction   ?          ?
low-conviction    ?          ?
```

If only clustered low-conviction has edge → classical theory.
If only isolated high-conviction has edge → our deployed pattern.
If both quadrants positive → the signal is robust regardless (rare).

Most signals will be in only one quadrant. Pre-classify by SNR first, then choose iso vs clu.

⚠️ **`RECALL_TRUST_MODE="production"` is not a defined trust mode, and it works by accident.**
`TrustPolicy.from_env` recognises exactly one value, `development` (after `strip().lower()`), and
treats everything else as **strict** — a deliberate design so that a misspelling cannot open the
gate. So `"production"` resolves to strict, which is the intended outcome, but it resolves there by
falling through rather than by naming anything. `RECALL_ENV`, separately, IS load-bearing and must
be `production` for the generation path. Two variables, similar values, only one of which is read
for its content. Verified 2026-08-25:
`python -c "from recall.trust_policy import TrustPolicy; print(TrustPolicy.from_env({'RECALL_TRUST_MODE':'production'}))"`

1. **`gone_from_disk` deleted rows for files that still existed.** `Path.exists()` on Python ≥3.12
   delegates to a C accelerator that swallows every `OSError`, so the `except OSError` beside it
   was unreachable and EACCES/EIO/ESTALE read as "deleted" — under the 50% prune guard, exit 0.
   Detail + the general trap → [[feedback-exercise-the-detection-path-not-the-green-path-2026-07-22]] §6.
2. **The `mcp` floor was still wrong after #65 raised it.** `>=1.10` is necessary, not sufficient:
   the tenant rides in `AccessToken.claims`, added in **1.27.2**. The whole declared range
   1.10–1.27.1 installs cleanly and dies on every authenticated call. Also `pgvector>=0.3` →
   `>=0.4` (`from pgvector import Vector` is a 0.4.0 export).

## What to reuse

Mid-audit a parallel session ran `git reset` on the shared worktree and **discarded every
uncommitted `.py`/`.toml`/`.lock` change**; untracked files survived. The branch was then rebuilt
(#65, #66 merged) underneath the running review, so an agent's report of "the tree changed under
me" was accurate and I wrongly dismissed it as a hallucination. Recovery came from a `git diff`
patch saved to the scratchpad.

**How to apply:** when a long agent-driven pass is running, (a) snapshot `git diff` + untracked
files to the scratchpad before any gate, (b) commit early rather than holding a large uncommitted
tree, (c) treat "the file changed under me" from a subagent as a fact to verify, not noise, and
(d) check `git reflog` first when work disappears — it names the operation.

## Delivery

Re-running the index-pressure arm at the **same seed** three times moved STR baseline across
**0.46 / 0.82 / 0.92**, coverage 0.01 ↔ 0.14, p50 latency 5.5 / 18.3 / 67.2 ms. The seed fixes
everything the project controls; it does not fix pgvector's HNSW build, and `hashing-64` puts
almost no signal in the vector, so the graph decides the outcome. **STR trust was 0.00 in all
three** — the claim that arm defends is untouched. FINDINGS §5b now publishes the spread.
Do not cite Arm B baseline/coverage/latency as point estimates.

Separately, `p50/p95/p99` were reported one rank too high (`int(q*n)` used as a 0-based index *is*
the 1-based nearest rank): p99 of 100 samples returned the max. Two copies of the formula, both
wrong. The fix moves a percentile by exactly one rank when `q*n` is an integer and is a no-op
otherwise — it does **not** explain the swings above.

## ⚠️ Two Claude sessions in one worktree will destroy each other's work

- **CI `floor` job** (`--resolution lowest-direct`, Python 3.11, full suite vs real pgvector).
  Verified in both directions: green at corrected floors, **red** at the old `mcp>=1.10`. It found
  the `pgvector` floor bug *and* a latent order-dependent test failure before it was committed.
- **`configure_logging()` sets `propagate = False` globally and never undoes it** — right in a
  process (a propagated record could reach stdout and corrupt MCP JSON-RPC), fatal in a test
  session: after the first test that calls it, `caplog` sees nothing from `recall.*`. Fixed with
  an autouse snapshot fixture in `tests/conftest.py`, not by pinning past a pytest that hides it.

## Benchmark numbers: Arm B is not reproducible, and was published as if it were

RE-call is **not installed on VPS2** — verified this session (`rg recall /etc/systemd/system` → 0
hits). Merging IS the delivery; no deploy step. Bench lives at `/opt/recall-bench`; never test
against the `recall_bench` DB.

# Report machine state; the spending judgement is not mine (2026-08-08)

**What I said.** A rented GPU sat idle after one 8-minute pass. I told the user it was "billing for
nothing".

**The correction**, verbatim: *"you need to be careful when you say is a waste of money."*

**Three things wrong with it, in order of how much they matter:**

1. **It is not my characterisation to make.** I do not know the hourly rate, the budget, or how the
   user weighs an idle box against the convenience of one being up. "Waste" asserts a judgement
   about someone else's money from data I do not have. The factual form — *"it is idle, here is the
   work available for it"* — carries the same information and leaves the decision where it belongs.

2. **The idle time was MINE.** I ran one pass and queued nothing behind it, with the next input
   already built and sitting on VPS2. Framing my own sequencing gap as a cost problem puts it on
   the wrong side of the ledger, and quietly transfers a failure I caused onto the user's spending.

3. 🔑 **Cost framing invites abrupt action, and abrupt action loses data.** The user destroyed the
   instance while an `scp` to it was in flight. That one was an upload, so nothing was lost. Had it
   been a download of a result that existed only on that box, it would have been gone.

**How to apply.**

- Report machine state plainly: what is running, what is idle, what work exists for it.
- Say explicitly when something is **safe to tear down**, and say when it is not, because the
  moment you mention cost the natural next action is to kill it.
- Never label the user's spend. If a cost fact is genuinely decision-relevant, give the number and
  the option, not the verdict.
- Queue work so a rented resource has continuous input rather than waiting on me to notice a job
  finished. Shipped as `scripts/gpu_score_queue.sh`: runs every pending pass back to back, skips
  absent inputs and completed outputs, and does not let one failure strand the rest.

**`pilot-003-deepseek` and `pilot-004-placebo` dollar figures are not directly comparable.** They
were computed on different price bases, and neither `costs.json` recorded which one it used.

- `pilot-003-deepseek`: the **frozen preregistration 002 rates**, 0.0574 / 0.1148 per Mtok.
- `pilot-004-placebo`: **`scripts/pilot.py`'s argparse defaults**, 0.05866 / 0.11732.

Found on 2026-08-29 while recomputing costs for the cache-read fix, not by looking for it. The
token counts reproduced exactly (pilot-004 sums to its recorded **9,386,264** metered tokens), but
the dollars were off by a uniform factor of **1.0219** across all four arms, which is exactly
`0.05866 / 0.0574`. Recomputing pilot-004 at the defaults reproduces its published per-arm figures
to four decimal places on every

reproduces its published per-arm figures
to four decimal places on every arm and the total.

**Why nothing caught it:** the artifact stored `pricing_as_of` and `pricing_model` but never the
prices, so recovering the basis meant reverse-solving a 2x2 linear system from two arms' rounded
totals. The run was launched without explicit `--price-in` / `--price-out` and silently took the
defaults, which had drifted from the frozen values.

**Fixed forward.** `ArmCosts.to_dict` publishes `usd_per_mtok_input`, `usd_per_mtok_output`, the
cache rates and `priced_cache_separately`, so this cannot recur silently (PR #9, `63ce4b5`).

## Maker rebates (maker-rebates)
- `fee_equivalent = C · feeRate · p · (1 − p)`  (C = shares filled, p = fill price, feeRate = category taker rate)
- `rebate = (your_fee_equivalent / total_fee_equivalent) · rebate_pool`
- Crypto: taker `feeRate = 0.07`, **rebate share 20%** (`rebateRate=0.2`, matches live `feeSchedule`). Sports–Tech 25%. Geopolitics fee-free.
- Paid **daily in pUSD, $1 min**. Eligibility = your maker order is FILLED (taken).
- Key shape: fee curve `p·(1−p)` is **max at p=0.5, ~0 at extremes** → rebate value is highest mid-price, near-worthless near 0/1.

## Two income streams (do NOT conflate)
- **Liquidity Rewards (LRP)** — paid for *resting two-sided quotes near mid*, **sampled, NO fill required**.
- **Maker Rebates** — paid only when your resting order **gets filled** (your liquidity is TAKEN), weighted by a fee curve.
- **Makers are NEVER charged fees** (`feeSchedule.takerOnly=true`). Taker fees fund the rebate pool. → a pure-maker two-sided fill collects the FULL `1 − combined_bid`; the only cost is adverse selection (NOT a maker fee). This corrects the old "spread eaten by fees" framing.

## LRP scoring (liquidity-rewards)
Per resting order: **S(v,s) = ((v − s)/v)² · b**
- `v` = max spread from midpoint in **cents** = per-market `rewardsMaxSpread` (= `max_incentive_spread`; observed **4.5¢** on 5m/15m BTC/ETH).
- `s` = your order's spread (cents) from the size-cutoff-adjusted midpoint. `s ≥ v` ⇒ score 0.
- `b` = in-game multiplier (sports live-game boost; **crypto updown b≈1**).
- Order must be ≥ `rewardsMinSize` (= `min_incentive_size`; observed **50 shares**) to qualify.

Two sided-scores (Up=market m, Down=complement m'):
- `Q_one` = bids on m + asks on m'
- `Q_two` = asks on m + bids on m'

**Every existing test created the directory in its own fixture.** `root = tmp_path / "project";

the bug is "nothing creates X", assert on an X that has deliberately never been created, and say

## Why it matters more than it sounds

🔑 **The tell I missed: the growth I plotted was the defence warming up, not the attack scaling.**
The mitigation has an activation threshold, so below it you see honest exponential growth and above
it a wall. Sampling only the region below the threshold produces a curve that is real, reproducible,
and points exactly the wrong way. That is a general shape, not an expat quirk: rate limiters, quota
checks and circuit breakers all look like "no effect" until they engage.

it a wall. Sampling only the region below the threshold produces a curve that is real, reproducible,
and points exactly the wrong way. That is a general shape, not an expat quirk: rate limiters, quota
checks and circuit breakers all look like "no effect" until they engage.

## Reusable test template

For ANY new shadow candidate, run a 3-quadrant test:

```
                 isolated    clustered
high-conviction   ?          ?
low-conviction    ?          ?
```

If only clustered low-conviction has edge → classical theory.
If only isolated high-conviction has edge → our deployed pattern.
If both quadrants positive → the signal is robust regardless (rare).

Most signals will be in only one quadrant. Pre-classify by SNR first, then choose iso vs clu.

## Lesson Learned

### 1. innerHTML vs DOM methods
I hook di sicurezza bloccano innerHTML. Usare sempre `createElement` + `textContent` per prevenire XSS. Le funzioni innerHTML-based (`renderSignalRow`, `renderScore`, etc.) sono state rimosse come dead code nella code review.

### 4. Flask non carica .env automaticamente
Python/Flask non legge i file `.env`. Serve un parser custom all'avvio (10 righe) oppure python-dotenv. Il parser custom evita dipendenze extra.

### 5. Sicurezza — Bind su Tailscale
`app.run(host="0.0.0.0")` espone la dashboard sull'IP pubblico. **Sempre** bindare su `100.123.176.54` (Tailscale). La variabile `DASHBOARD_HOST` permette override.

### 6. API Key — sessionStorage > localStorage
localStorage persiste tra sessioni e e' accessibile a XSS. sessionStorage e' piu' sicuro (scade alla chiusura tab). L'API key viene passata via URL la prima volta (`?api_key=...`), salvata in sessionStorage, e l'URL viene pulito con `replaceState`.

distribution. A fact term that is a rare phrase ("byte-identical prefix") costs nothing. A fact
term that is a common English word quietly makes every ordinary document mentioning it
unusable, and the shortfall is invisible in an aggregate.

gain is unattributable between "LLM helped" and "smaller units helped", (c) a document-corpus arm —

# Trading Economics — valutazione 2026-04-18

## Pricing (da utente)

## Analisi per use case "FRED consensus backfill"

### Basic $29/mo → ❌ inutile

### Standard $199/mo ($149 annuale) → ❌ non copre il bisogno

- **MA "Economic Calendar NOT AVAILABLE"** nella tier Standard!
  - Economic Calendar = proprio i dati actual+consensus+previous che ci servono
  - Calendar API richiede tier superiore (World/Enterprise, listino non pubblico, tipicamente $500-2000+/mo)
- Cosa otterremmo: indicatori aggregati + Financial Markets (prezzi, ma abbiamo già yfinance) + TE Forecasts (forecast proprietari di TE, ≠ street consensus)

## Possibili vantaggi non considerati

**Ragioni**:
- Basic = zero valore automazione
- Standard non include Calendar API (il dato che ci serve)
- Forward-only cron ($0) colma il gap in 6 mesi naturalmente
- Per il budget ($199/mo = $2388/anno) meglio riservare a FMP upgrade post-gate 2026-07-17

## Why: forward-only è superiore a ogni tier TE a parità di scopo
- Costruisce dataset proprio, no lock-in vendor
- Nessun rischio "tier higher required" dopo aver pagato
- Consensus capturato da fonti primarie (CNBC, MarketWatch) già usate nel progetto

1. **TE Forecasts** (non street consensus ma simili) — Standard li esporta. Potrebbero servire come *proxy* consensus se lo street consensus non è accessibile. ⚠️ Ma TE forecasts sono modellati da loro economisti, drift rispetto a Dow Jones/Bloomberg survey
2. **Mobile alerts** (Basic+) — alert push su release → noi già abbiamo Telegram custom. Zero valore aggiunto
3. **Forecasts Excel addon** — workflow ibrido: Excel scarica ogni lunedì, CSV → upload a VPS. Ma Standard $149/mo solo per questo è caro vs forward-only gratis

## Verdict 2026-04-18: **SKIP**

## How to apply: quando rivalutare
- Solo se forward-only mostra edge p<0.05 a Q4 2026 E scaling richiede backfill storico >5 anni (es. regime modeling long-horizon)
- Prima chiedere pricing Enterprise/World con Calendar API incluso (probabilmente $500+/mo, comparabile a Bloomberg Terminal $2k)
- Alternativa: negoziare FMP Premium upgrade (include economic calendar) invece di TE separato

**Why**: 2026-04-20 abbiamo scoperto un "edge" N1 "10-Q bullish May": N=160, WR 58.8%, ret +4.75%, perm p<0.0001, IS+4.65→OOS+4.99 (apparente stabilità). Sembrava solido. Poi scoperto che **tutte le 160 osservazioni erano del solo 2025**. Il "walk-forward IS/OOS" era solo early-May vs late-May dello stesso anno — non cross-year.
Test di controllo su SPY 2010-2025 ha mostrato che early-May+20d = **-0.21% vs baseline altri mesi** (t-stat 0.97, non significativo). L'intero "edge" era 2024 (+5.54%) + 2025 (+6.48%) bull-market beta su 10-Q timing.

**How to apply**:
1. Per ogni slice temporale (month/quarter/year/week), eseguire `GROUP BY EXTRACT(YEAR FROM filing_date) cnt` PRIMA di validare.
2. Richiedere N≥3 anni con N≥20 each per considerare l'edge validabile.
3. Per edge sospetti, test di controllo: run SPY-only sul periodo → se SPY-only dà gran parte del ret, è beta di calendario.
4. alpha_return è più affidabile di ret assoluto per stagionalità (meno confounded con bull-market drift).

**Related lessons**:
- [project_historical_results.md] pre-patch edge inflated da regime bull 2024-2025
- [feedback_rigorous_validation.md] Bonferroni + perm + bootstrap + confounding
- [feedback_validation_first.md] walk-forward cross-regime mandatory

# Seasonal Single-Year Trap

**Regola**: quando un'analisi slice rivela un edge su month-of-year, quarter, o qualsiasi ciclo stagionale, prima di investigarlo serve **verificare la copertura anni del dataset**. Se copre 1-2 anni → edge NON validabile, sospendere.

moment its findings are applied. The fix set is itself an unaudited diff, and it is written under
time pressure by someone who has just been told they were wrong, which is not the state in which

On 2026-08-16 I launched a bug audit in the background, watched CI go green, and
merged. The audit returned **ten findings, three high severity**, fourteen
minutes after the merge. Two were regressions the merged change had introduced,
and one was the only *permanent* failure state in the mechanism: a lock that
could not be reclaimed and that the code itself could create.

**Why CI did not catch any of it.** Every check passed: schema migrations on
three Postgres versions, typecheck, audit, floor, and the full suite. CI ran the
tests that existed. All three high-severity defects were in paths **no test
covered**, which is exactly what an adversarial audit is for and exactly what a
green pipeline cannot tell you. **Green CI means "no known regression", never
"reviewed".**

- They disagreed on **199 answerable questions**, and the user hand-labelled **195** of them blind to arbitrate — `benchmarks/labelling/` (built 2026-07-24), whose own README says hand-labelling *"arbitrates between the judges directly"*.
- A separate audit measured `gpt-4o-mini` accepting **62.81%** of deliberately wrong-but-on-topic answers — `benchmarks/PREREGISTRATION.md`: *"it rewards vagueness"*.

So the human was the ground truth all along, and the paid judge was the thing being graded. **It did not remove the work — it created 199 items of it, and carried a measured 63% error rate on adversarial cases.**

## How to apply

scelta per ordine di inserimento**: `next(iter(cutoffs))` poteva confrontare il `top_50` di Mem0 col nostro `k=200`. Il "tell" era già nel tree — `build_beam_labelling.py` fissava `top_200`: due lettori dello stesso file di terze parti in disaccordo, e solo uno poteva avere ragione.

## Il mio punto cieco — vale più dei finding

**Final standing decision (do NOT re-open without fundamentally new corpus)**:
- v6 pipeline is dead on this corpus / chase-deterministic dataset.
- The 2026-05-04 audit identified 8+2 real bugs and the fixes are all valid (verified by clean PEFT load + temporal split). The PROBLEM is upstream: even with correctly trained heads, Phase 4 features extract no out-of-sample signal from SEC filings beyond what v5 already captures via composite_score / lexicon / claude_score.
- Pattern recurring (4th time): SFT v1/v2/v3, 14B scaling, BGE-M3 contrastive, RLVR v1/v2, Phase 4 heads — all show ΔBrier in noise band when tested rigorously.
- Cost summary across both days: ~$8 vast compute total (Phase 3b runs + v6.1 backfill).

- **After building a verifier, run its own motivating defect back through it.** One line. The sign
  case was a `scan_text(...)` call away the whole time.
- **When a checker has two views of the same input, prove the views agree.** Masked-for-numbers vs
  raw-for-markers is where P1-B lived. Any "extract A from view 1, B from view 2, then relate A and
  B" shape deserves an explicit test that a thing hidden in one view cannot act through the other.
- **Complexity concentrates where value doesn't.** The `derived:` marker had **zero production uses**
  (7 markers total across four documents: 6 `withdrawn`, 1 `citation-pending`, 0 `artifact`,
  0 `derived`) yet generated three of the nine findings — an AST walker, a length bound, a recursion
  catch, a rounding convention. Count the live

A fourth, found the same way by another session: a monkeypatch still targeting
`_find_manifest_path` after the function became `_find_manifest_paths`. It intercepted nothing while
the test passed. Proved by mutating the real handler to `return name, "MUTATED"` and watching the
test stay green.

**Why:** a test that cannot fail is byte-identical, in every report and every diff, to one that
passes. Green is the same colour either way. Reading tells you what a test *says*; only breaking the
thing it guards tells you whether it is *attached* to it.

Due dei 12 "P3" erano bug di correttezza: `_gold` leggeva la chiave `"nugget"` mentre BEAM usa `"description"` (mostrava un **dict repr grezzo** all'annotatore umano come gold standard), e `--limit` applicato dopo lo shuffle tagliava le coppie di arm a metà ⇒ le due accuracy per-arm calcolate su **insiemi di domande diversi** e stampate affiancate come confronto.
Il "performance" item valeva 47 min/run: `collapse()` era O(k²) puro-Python, **47,5 s per domanda → 0,057 s**, verificato **byte-identico** contro una re-implementazione indipendente (30 corpora × 4 soglie + vettore-zero), non solo più veloce.
Il parser `--conversations` esisteva **7 volte** in 2 varianti in disaccordo (le copie inline omettevano `.strip()`).

## Aperto / non fatto

**STANDING DECISION (do not re-open without new info)**:
- v6 pipeline (Phase 3a + Phase 4 heads + Stacker v6) does NOT add value over v5
- The 4 closed paths together: SFT v1/v2/v3 (3 attempts), 14B scaling, BGE-M3 contrastive,
  Phase 3b RLVR v1/v2, Phase 4 heads + Stacker v6 — all FAIL on this corpus / dataset.
- Pattern recurring: chase corpus → SFT memorization → no signal extraction
- Consistent with CLAUDE.md "Fine-tuning ABANDONED" decision (2026-04-21).
- **Re-opening only if**: (a) new corpus that breaks chase determinism, OR (b) heads
  retrained on properly-loaded `qwen7b-domain-base` adapter with leakage audit, OR
  (c) different aspect heads with deterministic non-leaking labels.

**Why:** reviewing a guard tends to check "does this correctly implement the rule?" rather than

  ACCEPTED. A guard built to catch "a wrong number reads as fluently as a right one" was blind to
  the canonical instance of exactly that.
- **Markers laundered numbers.** Numbers were extracted from the *masked* text; markers from the
  *raw* text. A marker written inside backticks — the natural way to document the marker syntax —
  bound to whatever real number preceded it and marked it cited. With `citation-pending` that
  required no artifact at all, and the number never reached the ratchet, so it was invisible twice.

**The decisive fact is not the dollar figure, it is who can see it.** `IngestReport` carries
`llm_input_tokens`/`llm_output_tokens` for a hosted-extraction arm and `local_model` for a local
one; a SaaS that extracts on its own infrastructure reports NEITHER, so its bill never reaches the

# Restore drill database boundary

The scheduled Aurora restore drill is a database recovery check. The validator discovers every
public table with a `tenant_id` column and requires forced row level security, a tenant policy, and
`SELECT` for the serving role across that set. It still does not start the MCP application or make
an authenticated HTTP request through OIDC, authorization, rate limiting, retrieval, and response
serialization.

Keep operational documentation explicit about this boundary until a separate application smoke
task is wired to the restored cluster.

# VPS3 PostgreSQL ~3.5h outage 2026-06-27 + DB watchdog

**Incident:** postgres (`postgresql@16-main`, VPS3) crashed into automatic recovery
at **~02:14 UTC** (backend crash → postmaster reset → recovery; systemd saw NO stop,
`NRestarts=0`). It sat **REFUSING connections for ~3.5h** (02:14→05:46), so the ENTIRE
trading stack errored `OperationalError: connection refused` (~9k errors: updown,
copytrade, fairvalue, hawkes, gabigol-probe crash-looping). Recovered only when the
**user manually `systemctl restart postgresql@16-main` at 05:46:30** (redo clean 0.13s,
"ready to accept connections"). No clear cause in PG log / no kernel OOM around 02:14 →
likely an abrupt backend kill or host (Contabo) hiccup; **RAM is chronically tight
(~60Mi free / 7.6G, mixed pg+python)** = standing risk.

# Restore checksum validation is bounded by default

The Aurora restore drill hashes at most 10,000 rows per validated table by default, ordered by
the primary key of `recall_chunks_v1` or `recall_generations`. The receipt records the mode, row
bound, and per table durations. This keeps checksum work bounded as the corpus grows, but it can
miss corruption outside the deterministic prefix. Set `RECALL_RESTORE_CHECKSUM_MODE=full` for an
explicit high assurance drill that hashes every visible row. Expected checksums must be generated
with the same mode and bound. The change was made in commit `7c04f8bd` after the restore review
identified full table hashing as a possible RTO cost.

## Convergence as N grew (mean reversion)

# Restore drill database boundary

The scheduled Aurora restore drill is a database recovery check. The validator discovers every
public table with a `tenant_id` column and requires forced row level security, a tenant policy, and
`SELECT` for the serving role across that set. It still does not start the MCP application or make
an authenticated HTTP request through OIDC, authorization, rate limiting, retrieval, and response
serialization.

Keep operational documentation explicit about this boundary until a separate application smoke
task is wired to the restored cluster.

# Restore checksum validation is bounded by default

The Aurora restore drill hashes at most 10,000 rows per validated table by default, ordered by
the primary key of `recall_chunks_v1` or `recall_generations`. The receipt records the mode, row
bound, and per table durations. This keeps checksum work bounded as the corpus grows, but it can
miss corruption outside the deterministic prefix. Set `RECALL_RESTORE_CHECKSUM_MODE=full` for an
explicit high assurance drill that hashes every visible row. Expected checksums must be generated
with the same mode and bound. The change was made in commit `7c04f8bd` after the restore review
identified full table hashing as a possible RTO cost.

# VPS3 PostgreSQL ~3.5h outage 2026-06-27 + DB watchdog

**Incident:** postgres (`postgresql@16-main`, VPS3) crashed into automatic recovery
at **~02:14 UTC** (backend crash → postmaster reset → recovery; systemd saw NO stop,
`NRestarts=0`). It sat **REFUSING connections for ~3.5h** (02:14→05:46), so the ENTIRE
trading stack errored `OperationalError: connection refused` (~9k errors: updown,
copytrade, fairvalue, hawkes, gabigol-probe crash-looping). Recovered only when the
**user manually `systemctl restart postgresql@16-main` at 05:46:30** (redo clean 0.13s,
"ready to accept connections"). No clear cause in PG log / no kernel OOM around 02:14 →
likely an abrupt backend kill or host (Contabo) hiccup; **RAM is chronically tight
(~60Mi free / 7.6G, mixed pg+python)** = standing risk.

**Real gap:** nothing alerted or auto-recovered a multi-hour DB outage. Fixed:

fail x2 (~4min) → ONE Telegram alert; fail x3+ (~6min) → `systemctl restart
postgresql@16-main` + Telegram. Runs as **root** (postgres restart NOT in sentiment
sudo allowlist). State in /run; silent when healthy. Reads TELEGRAM_* from .env by key.

`auc_rmax`, which the note covers at 0.010.

## What it surfaced on day one

one ranked card per axis, then five-column tables with the other seven fields behind a per-row
disclosure that opens automatically on disputed and rejected rows.

  the row the axis trusts least — the "retrieve nothing, leak nothing, score 0.0000" vector the

existing guard called `_fmt_figures_with_status` directly, so

  ranked plus one rejected read as "all 3 runs are tied" above four visible rows. Fixed by naming

## Fix (commit 0a5a326, branch fix/equity-stale-f2-incident)
1. `ftmo/broker/ctrader.py`: `_PRICE_FRESHNESS_MAX_SEC: 8h → 18h`
   - Covers weekday overnight (Tue-Fri 21:00 UTC → next 13:30 UTC ≈ 16h)
   - Still rejects weekend (Fri close → Mon open ≈ 64h, well above 18h)
2. `ftmo/risk/circuit_breaker.py` equity_stale escalation policy:
   - Threshold 10 → 30 ticks (~30 min)
   - REMOVED `should_close_all=True` on stale escalation
   - REMOVED `TRADING_HALTED` latch on stale escalation
   - Stays at `WARN`, `can_open=False` (block new), auto-recovers on first healthy tick

**Why:** 2026-05-13 ~22:22 UTC `ftmo-min-days-insurance@F4` crashed AFTER
the insurance trade had completed (entry filled, position closed). The
post-close `broker.get_positions()` call raised:
`cTrader response type mismatch: expected ProtoOAReconcileRes, got
ProtoOAExecutionEvent (payloadType=2126)`. cTrader had emitted a late
ExecutionEvent for the just-closed position; the ctrader-open-api SDK's
Deferred-routing handed it to the next sync caller instead of the message
handler. The trade itself succeeded — only the post-trade reconcile died,
producing a false `failed` systemd state.

Expected: `account <ctid_from_step_4> auth OK` + `eq=$10,000.00` lines, NO `CTID MISMATCH`. If `CTID MISMATCH` appears, the service goes into `failed` state after 3 retries (per `StartLimitBurst=3 / StartLimitIntervalSec=300` in base unit) — **do NOT bypass; investigate cred file**.

```sql
SELECT * FROM ftmo_account_health WHERE account_id='F6';
-- expected: status='OK', expected_ctid = connected_ctid
```

### 12. Open GH gate issue

At 06:00 UTC (8h after US close, low-volume Asian/EU session):

# FTMO ARC fails CLOSED (2026-07-14) — PR #1860, deployed VPS2

## The bug

ARC gates position opening/sizing on a market-stress score (VIX etc. via yfinance). If the **startup** stress probe couldn't score (yfinance down / rate-limited / cold-cache `database is locked`), `ftmo/main.py` hand-built an `ArcAction` with `can_open_new=True, sizing_multiplier=1.0, exposure_level=FULL` and entered the main loop with it.

**On zero visibility into market stress, the live prop account traded at FULL SIZE with gating OFF.** The old comment said the quiet part out loud: *"so trading isn't blocked by a transient DNS/rate-limit issue"* — trading a bounded cost (a few missed entries) for an unbounded one (an unguarded entry into a stress event).

retries (not silent) |
| `ProtoOAErrorRes` on `get_account()` for new account, but `is_available()`=True | Challenge purchased but no first trade yet → FTMO trader entity not provisioned | Place 1 manual trade (step 8) |
| Multiple services see same position IDs (e.g. 52375329 across F3+F4+F5) | All cred files point to same cTrader account | Re-OAuth + re-discover |
| Grafana "Accounts — Health & Truth" shows MISMATCH | Live ctid ≠ expected — investigate `/home/sentiment/ctrader_credentials.<acc>.env` immediately | Don't restart blindly; correlate with `ftmo_equity_log.broker_ctid` history |

## Files / configs that MUST be in lockstep

**Why it costs more than it should:** the error names a schema, not a cause, and it fires on tests
that have nothing to do with the script. The first time I read it as a defect in the test file I
had just written.

**How to apply.** Either give a measurement its own database, or reset between:

```bash
bash scripts/session-db.sh down && bash scripts/session-db.sh up
```

Two seconds, and it puts the container back where conftest expects it. Prefer resetting **after**
the measurement rather than before the suite, so the wrong state never outlives the run that
created it.

🔑 The general form: **a shared fixture that is global rather than per-test is the one a script can
poison**, and the poisoning surfaces somewhere else entirely. `make_store`'s uuid-named tables are
immune; `recall_chunks_v1`, `recall_generations` and `recall_calibrations` are not.

Related: [[concurrent-pytest-false-reds]], which is the same shape from contention rather than from
schema width.

2026-09-01/02, twice in one session. A script measuring the certifying floor used
`resolve_embedder("fastembed")` (384 dimensions) against this checkout's session container. The
next `pytest` run failed at **setup, in every test of the file**:

```
recall.schema.SchemaIncompatible: recall_chunks_v1 uses vector(384), requested dimension is 64
```

`tests/conftest.py` provisions at **dim 64** (`apply_migrations(TEST_DSN, table="chunks", dim=64)`),
and the generation tables are global rather than per-test — `make_store` hands out a throwaway
table per test, but `recall_chunks_v1` is shared. So a measurement and the suite cannot both use
one container unless they agree on the width.

| guidance_low_uncert | 6/41 | -8.21 | [-19.29, +2.87] | 0.146 | INCONCLUSIVE |

| mgmt_conf_HI | 15/32 | -4.30 | [-14.16, +5.56] | 0.392 | INCONCLUSIVE |

**Findings**:

1. **0/8 factor passa gate causale rigoroso a N=47**.

2. **Direzioni suggestive** (consistente con underpromise-overdeliver hypothesis):
   - `outlook_vague` POSITIVO (+5.04%): hedged language → outperformance
   - `outlook_specific` NEGATIVO (-8.94%): specific commitments → underperformance
   - `mgmt_conf_HI` NEGATIVO (-4.30%): over-confident management → underperformance
   - `guidance_low_uncert` NEGATIVO (-8.21%): low hedging → underperformance
   - **Pattern coerente**: 4 fattori indipendenti puntano alla stessa narrativa "underpromise-overdeliver"

3. **N=47 troppo piccolo** per power statistico. CI larghi (~±10%). Versione iniziale (no dedup) mostrava p<0.005 ma era artefatto di rows duplicate per `run_id` (3x inflated dataset → 141 rows).

**Pairwise Cramer's V matrix** (collinearity tra factor):
- `guidance_low_uncert ↔ outlook_specific`: V=**0.94** (quasi identici!)
- `mgmt_conf_LO ↔ comp_intense`: V=0.53 (moderata)
- `mgmt_conf_LO ↔ supply_strained_critical`: V=0.45 (moderata)
- Other pairs: V<0.30 (weak)

| Factor | Uni ATE/p | Multi ATE/p | Status |
|--------|-----------|-------------|--------|
| **supply_strained_critical** | +6.36/0.020 | **+5.34/0.044** | ✅ INDIPENDENTE |
| **comp_intense** | +6.32/0.013 | **+5.20/0.041** | ✅ INDIPENDENTE |
| mgmt_conf_LO | +7.70/0.026 | +4.90/0.182 | ⚠ MEDIATO |
| guidance_low_uncert | -7.27/0.034 | -3.52/0.294 | ⚠ MEDIATO |
| outlook_specific | -7.81/0.033 | -5.30/0.123 | ⚠ MEDIATO |

3. **Interpretazione**: "underpromise-overdeliver" classico. Riconoscimento trasparente di problemi = signal di credibility → market rewards. Over-promising = signal di over-extension → market punishes.

4. **Bonferroni**: α=0.006 (8 test), 0/8 passano strictly. Single-test α=0.05: 5/8 pass (chiaramente robusti). Would need N≥300 per Bonferroni.

**Caveats**:
- Factor potenzialmente correlati (mgmt_conf_LO ↔ supply_strained? comp_intense?). Multivariate DML non fatto.
- Assenza di interactions testing (es. mgmt_conf_LO × supply_strained).
- Sector confounding partial (LightGBM OH encoding gestisce ma small N per sector × factor).

**Lezione meta**: PRIMA di integrare un set di factor in un filter, sempre testare independence multivariate. 5 factor univariate-significant ≠ 5 driver indipendenti. Cramer's V + DML controlling for others = test diagnostico essenziale.

## The fix

1. **Blind data must never WIDEN risk.** Degrade → block new risk; never fail open "so trading isn't blocked". (Restates the 04-29 lesson; this is its second violation.)
2. **A fail-closed change makes silence dangerous.** Before the fix, a broken alert was cosmetic. After, it's the only thing standing between you and a silently-halted account. **When you change a system from fail-open to fail-closed, audit its alerting in the same commit.**
3. **A source-text assertion is not a test.** The old test asserted the *string* `'arc_startup_yfinance_failed'` appeared in `run()`'s source — it passed with the bug fully intact. Replaced with behavioral tests; mutation-verified (restore `can_open_new=True` → the test fails).

**`RECALL_OIDC_SUBJECT_TENANTS` CONSTRAINS the tenant claim, it does not SUPPLY it.** I assumed it
let the deployment name the tenant and skip the claim. It does not: the token must still carry

means the IdP must emit the claim — and on Keycloak 24+ that additionally needs **unmanaged
attributes enabled on the realm's user profile**, or the attribute is silently dropped and the
token carries `tenant: null`.

**The audience must equal the client id**, at least on Keycloak. `_check_authorized_party`
enforces OIDC Core 3.1.3.7 (a multi-audience token must name us in `azp`), Keycloak sets
`azp = client_id` and adds `account` to `aud` by default, so a custom audience string can never
match. The check is right: without it any other client of the same IdP holding a token that lists
our audience becomes a valid caller, and its `tenant` claim becomes the isolation boundary.

| # | Refusal | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `issuer must be an https:// URL` | `http://` issuer | real TLS, **no loopback exemption** |
| 2 | `invalid_grant: Account is not fully set up` | Keycloak's user profile wants more than a username | set email / first / last, clear required actions |
| 3 | `reason=bad_audience` | `azp != audience` on a multi-audience token | **set `RECALL_OIDC_AUDIENCE` to the CLIENT ID** |
| 4 | `reason=missing_tenant` | no `tenant` claim in the token | user attribute + attribute mapper |
| 5 | `PermissionError: this token lacks ...` | no `recall:*` scopes | client scopes `recall:read` / `recall:write`, attached as defaults |

Three that are worth keeping:

**`RECALL_OIDC_SUBJECT_TENANTS` CONSTRAINS the tenant claim, it does not SUPPLY it.** I assumed it
let the deployment name the tenant and skip the claim. It does not: the token must still carry
`tenant`, and the binding then refuses a subject not bound to it. That is the configuration to
prefer over `RECALL_OIDC_TRUST_TENANT_CLAIM` (the IdP asserts, the deployment constrains), but it
means the IdP must emit the claim — and on Keycloak 24+ that additionally needs **unmanaged
attributes enabled on the realm's user profile**, or the attribute is silently dropped and the
token carries `tenant: null`.

**Issuer must be HTTPS, checked at construction** (`recall_mcp/oidc.py`, `STAKES-003`), because
the later failure arrives as `jwks_unavailable` and sends an operator hunting a network fault for
a value that could never have worked. **So the OIDC path cannot be exercised against a plain-HTTP
local IdP at all** — any dev or CI environment testing auth needs real TLS. A self-signed cert
trusted through `SSL_CERT_FILE` for the server process only works, because
`urllib.request.build_opener` uses the default SSL context; nothing machine-wide changes.

`RECALL_OIDC_SUBJECT_TENANTS=sub:tenant,...` pins the mapping; a bound subject naming another
**provisioned** tenant is refused `subject_tenant_mismatch` on a genuine signed token. Checked
after the signature (else it enumerates subjects). The tenant is everything after the **LAST**
colon, so a k8s `system:serviceaccount:ns:sa` subject is bindable; a *forgotten* tenant is caught
by the allowed_tenants cross-check, not by the parser.

⚠️ **BREAKING: an OIDC deployment now refuses to boot until it answers.** Either pin the map, or
`RECALL_OIDC_TRUST_TENANT_CLAIM=1`. No default, because a default here is a fail-open.

Chosen: **explicit allowlist** (`RECALL_OIDC_TENANTS`, no default, absent ≠ "every tenant").
Rejected for now: open set with an LRU cap, which deletes the invariant and needs StoreRegistry work.

expiry moving to the IdP, never tenant enumeration.

## The design decision (asked, not assumed)

`StoreRegistry` takes a fixed `allowed_tenants` and documents that the tenant set comes from
configuration and **never from traffic**. OIDC has no enumerable tenant set (tenants arrive inside
tokens), so wiring it in without an allowlist would have deleted that property silently.

Also in #202: `RECALL_AUTH_MODE=oidc|static` makes the cutover staged. Only the SELECTED mechanism
is built (production refuses the token file, so loading both then choosing breaks the flip), but
the OIDC block is still VALIDATED when present so step 1 is a real rehearsal. 🔑 Two limits:
**step 1 cannot run under `RECALL_ENV=production`**, and **rollback is a mode flip only while the
token file still exists**.

## Reusable, verified this session

The refresh token was keyed by account from the first commit, with a docstring that said why:
*"so two accounts on one machine do not overwrite each other"*. The short-lived cache beside it
was a single global file. `access_token(config)` returns `cached_access_token()` **before it
looks at which account asked**, so:

1. A hook runs in a project configured for account A and caches A's access token.
2. Within that token's lifetime, a hook runs in a project configured for account B.
3. B's session gets A's bearer, uploads B's memos, and the server resolves the tenant **from the
   token**.
4. B's memories land in A's corpus. No error on either side. Both look successful.

**When one store in a credential flow is keyed by an identity, every store in that flow must be
keyed by the same identity. A disagreement between them is not untidiness, it is a leak, and it
cannot be detected from either end at runtime.**

Found 2026-09-01 in `recall_hooks/credentials.py`, on my own branch, during a review of my own
commit. Caught before merge; nothing shipped.

The shape, which is the reusable part:

| Store | Keyed by | Written when |
|---|---|---|
| refresh token (keyring or fallback file) | **account** | `login` |
| access token cache (`recall-hook-token.json`) | **nothing** | every refresh |

🔑 **The tell was the docstring, not the code.** One function explained why it was keyed by
account; the function four lines below it was not, and nothing reconciled the two. A comment
justifying a key is evidence that an identity matters in that flow, so **every other store in the
same flow is now a question**. That is a cheap grep and it is the one I did not do until review.

⛔ **Do not fix this with a default parameter.** My first instinct was
`cached_access_token(config=None)` so existing call sites kept working. A default puts every
caller that omits one back into a single shared bucket, which is the bug wearing a signature that
looks fixed. The parameter is required, and the three call sites were updated.

Two layers, because the path alone is not proof:

- the filename carries a **digest** of the account (a digest, so a directory listing does not hold
  somebody's email address);
- the account is written **into the payload**, and a read whose recorded account does not match is
  refused rather than used. Reaching that check means a hand-edited file or an older payload, and
  every reason to be there is a reason to fetch a fresh token instead.

**Cost of the lesson:** none, this time. It was found by reading my own diff after a green suite,
which is the only reason it is a memo rather than an incident. The suite was green because no test
had ever constructed two accounts: a leak between identities is invisible to a test suite that
only ever has one identity. **Where isolation is the property, the test needs two of the thing.**

**How to apply:** when any flow stores one secret in more than one place, list the stores and their
keys in a table before writing the second one. If the keys differ, either they are the same
identity under two names (say so in a comment) or you have found this bug. And write the test that
uses two identities, because that is the test the suite will not otherwise have.
